newsitem.title: SPAIN: ATHLETICS-MARATHON RUNNER SUSPENDED OVER DOPING ALLEGATIONS.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-MARATHON RUNNER SUSPENDED OVER DOPING ALLEGATIONS.

text.p: Pablo Sierra, one of Spain's leading marathon runners, has been suspended for six months after making allegations of drug taking, the Spanish athletics federation said on Wednesday.

Sierra recently alleged that world marathon champion Martin Fiz, his coach Sabino Padilla and Spanish athletics federation president Jose Maria Odriozola had colluded over drug taking by many of Spain's top marathon runners.
"The allegations were made without any evidence," a federation spokeswoman said.
The suspension took effect on Tuesday when Sierra acknowledged receipt of a letter informing him of the ban.
"President Odriozola and Sabino Padilla are also suing Pablo Sierra for libel following his comments," the spokeswoman said.
Padilla also coached former Tour de France cycling winner Miguel Indurain.
Sierra has a marathon best time of two hours 11 minutes 35 seconds and finished 12th in this year's London Marathon.
But he failed to gain a place in Spain's team for August's world championships.
Sierra has said he might go to the United States, where he trains regularly, and seek citizenship there.
